qbNote: Nick does not name one quarterback — his stated goal is to land any of the top 8 at a value: Allen, Lamar, Maye, Daniels, Burrow, Hurts, Caleb Williams, Herbert. Goff is the fallback if you pass on that range.

philosophy.title: Running backs early — the cliff is real
philosophy.text: His #1 2026 thesis: attack high-volume starting RBs early. 'Robust RB' / double-hero-RB (3 RBs in the first 4 rounds) is winning at a high rate. Starting NFL backs keep weekly value; backups ≈ zero. The late-round RB pool is a dead zone.

philosophy.title: Tight end: early or late, NEVER the middle
philosophy.text: 'Mid-round TE is a losing bet, year after year.' Pay up for an elite anchor (Bowers R2 / Loveland R4) OR wait and double-dip late (Kittle/Andrews/Kincaid). Avoid the round 6–10 TE range.

philosophy.title: Quarterback: elite value early OR wait to R5–7, then ride one
philosophy.text: Never QB in round 1 or 2. Elite QBs slipping on recency bias (Josh Allen) are fine value, but he prefers the R5–7 margins (Maye). THE MID-ROUND QB TRAP: if you miss the elite tier, do NOT pay up for the next sub-tier early (Dak/Herbert/Lawrence in R6) — wait to the absolute tail-end of that tier for the max discount (he took Trevor Lawrence at R8 in his 12-tm PPR mock). Pick one QB and ride him. Caveat: a full QB embargo R3–7 assumes no league-wide run — if your league panics you can get stuck streaming, so stay flexible.

philosophy.title: Don't stack teammates in redraft
philosophy.text: Negative correlation kills you in season-long (e.g. won't pair Ja'Marr Chase + Chase Brown, or 3 Chargers). Stacking is a best-ball play, not a redraft play.

philosophy.title: Rookies are mostly irrelevant in redraft
philosophy.text: Pass on deep rookies — only elite feature backs (Jeanty, Jeremiah Love) matter, and even those he'll fade if hype inflates the cost or the team is tanking.

philosophy.title: Playoff schedule & domes matter; fade tankers
philosophy.text: Target Lions/Saints/Eagles anchors for late-season dome games; fade open-air northern teams and brutal playoff slates (Eagles Wk15–17 vs SEA/HOU/SF). Fade tanking teams (Cardinals, Panthers) that bench young stars in the fantasy playoffs.

philosophy.title: Chase positive TD regression
philosophy.text: Target elite players with high red-zone/green-zone volume but unlucky TD totals (Justin Jefferson, Mike Evans, Tyler Warren) — TD luck is volatile and self-corrects.

philosophy.title: Value vs ADP discipline
philosophy.text: Don't reach — temper projections with market ADP; you can usually get your guy a round later.

philosophy.title: Single-flex roster balance — don't multiply too early
philosophy.text: In single-flex builds (MWV) keep RB/WR balanced early: don't take back-to-back WRs in Rounds 1–2. If a Round 3 RB run hits while you're WR-heavy, you're forced into sub-optimal builds. (RPB has NO flex at all, so early balance matters even more.)

philosophy.title: Tight end: wait, then double-dip athletic TEs on elite QBs
philosophy.text: In the 12-tm PPR mock he boycotted TE until the single-digit-ADP rounds, then double-dipped highly athletic profiles attached to elite/high-volume QBs (Kincaid–Buffalo, Gadsden–Chargers). Reinforces the 'early or late, never the middle' rule from the late side.

philosophy.title: Round 2 RBs — the league-wide decision point (half-PPR / RPB)
philosophy.text: From picks 3–12, UNLESS an elite faller is there (Brock Bowers, Drake London, or CeeDee Lamb / Justin Jefferson if they slip), take the RB — they all project similarly with heavy upside, so your RANKING is the edge. Nick's R2 RB board (half-PPR): 1) Saquon Barkley — easiest Wk1–14 SOS, ~300 touches, Patullo→Mannion play-call upgrade; 2) Kenneth Walker — big new contract, zero early-down competition, locked goal-line; 3) Chase Brown — elite pass-catcher (he'd be ABOVE Walker in full PPR), lower rush ceiling in 0.5; 4) Omarion Hampton — huge goal-line/TD upside, volume capped by Keaton Mitchell (watch camp); 5) Derrick Henry — dominant runner but fading targets = volatile 0.5 floor at 32; 6) De'Von Achane — AVOID: McDaniel gone, mobile Willis kills his target floor, hardest Wk13+ SOS. R1 RBs stay locked in pairs: Gibbs/Bijan → Taylor/CMC → Hall/Cook.
